Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right-sided paratracheal/superior mediastinal soft-tissue opacity with a lobulated contour, which is consistent with an esophageal lipoma; this diagnosis aligns with the patient's reported symptoms of dysphagia and dyspepsia due to mass effect on the esophagus. Other options like thymoma (anterior), neurogenic tumor (posterior), or calcified granuloma do not fit the location, density, or clinical presentation as accurately.
